name: Refik Anadol
bio: Refik Anadol (born 1985) is a media artist who works with large datasets and machine learning, turning archives of images, sound and sensor readings into moving 'data paintings' and 'data sculptures' at architectural scale. He studied in Istanbul and at UCLA's Design Media Arts programme and runs a studio in Los Angeles. WDCH Dreams (2018) projected the LA Philharmonic's digital archive onto the outside of the Walt Disney Concert Hall. The Machine Hallucinations series (from 2019) trains models on millions of photographs of cities, nature or space and then 'dreams' through what the model has learned. Unsupervised (2022–23) did this with MoMA's own collection in the museum's lobby. Other works use EEG recordings (Melting Memories, 2018) or wind data.
studyNotes: The dataset is the subject. Every work starts from a specific archive or sensor stream; ask what was collected, by whom, and what was left out.
Moving between images. The flowing forms are walks through the model's 'latent space', where one image morphs into another.
Architecture as a screen. Walls, buildings and rooms become displays; the site is part of the composition.
Scale and immersion. The work is designed for bodies standing in front of something huge; compare the experience with watching the same video on a laptop.
